summary: The agent implemented nearly all inherited-super-mapping behavior and preserved the baseline suite, but one new test failed because a three-way conflict diagnostic named only two of the three competing mapper types.
quick_failure_summary: A three-way inherited mapping conflict reports only two competing declaring mapper types.

details.reasoning: The implementation completes the feature and passes 102 of 103 new tests, but its conflict branch explicitly selects only the first and second most-specific declarations for the diagnostic. Therefore a conflict among Alpha, Beta, and Gamma omits Gamma, violating the requirement that the compilation error identify the declaring mapper types involved in the conflict.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's focused conflict test covered only two incomparable branches, so its validation did not exercise a conflict involving three or more mapper types. The added tests were legitimate feature tests, not test manipulation.

justification.issue_description: Conflict diagnostics do not list every mapper type contributing a competing mapping when more than two incomparable branches declare the same target.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires that competing mappings produce a compilation error that identifies the target and declaring mapper types. In processor/src/main/java/org/mapstruct/ap/internal/processor/MethodRetrievalProcessor.java:418-427, the agent takes only mostSpecific.get(0) and mostSpecific.get(1), and processor/src/main/java/org/mapstruct/ap/internal/util/Message.java:51 has exactly two mapper-type placeholders. The hidden test expected ThreeWayAlphaK7p4, ThreeWayBetaK7p4, and ThreeWayGammaK7p4, but the actual diagnostic omitted Gamma.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented-requirement or test-mismatch verdict because the prompt's plural requirement applies to all competing declaring mapper types; limiting the diagnostic to two is an implementation omission. It is also more specific than FAIL_WRONG_LOGIC because the failed behavior directly corresponds to an explicit requirement.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is demanding but fair: it precisely specifies inheritance precedence, diamond deduplication, flattening, generic override resolution, source rebinding, expression handling, diagnostics, and interaction with configuration inheritance. The sole failure checks a reasonably foreseeable multi-branch form of an explicitly stated diagnostic requirement.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 3649 baseline tests passed and 102 of 103 new tests passed.
The only new-test failure is a deterministic diagnostic-content assertion against the agent-modified conflict-reporting code.
The post-agent harness reported a three-way test.patch merge failure but reset the affected files, reapplied the test patch, and successfully executed all 103 new tests.

The trajectory shows minor missing-rg and patch-helper friction, but the agent recovered immediately, completed the implementation, ran focused tests successfully, and passed the broader verify command.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker affected the result; the isolated failure is explained by incomplete diagnostic aggregation in the implementation.
